text: The abdominal X-ray shows multiple dilated loops of bowel with air-fluid levels, but no gas is visible in the distal colon, which is highly suggestive of distal intestinal obstruction. To confirm the diagnosis and rule out meconium ileus or Hirschsprung disease, I need to visualize the anatomy further. REQUEST TEST: Contrast_Enema

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal contrast enema rules out meconium ileus and Hirschsprung disease, leaving duodenal atresia as the most likely cause of this proximal obstruction. REQUEST TEST: Upper_GI_Series

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal upper GI series rules out malrotation, so we must consider a more distal obstruction like jejunal or ileal atresia. Has the infant passed any meconium since birth? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound
